full_judgment:
5. Considering the evidence. on record, adduced by the prosecution and the defence version, the learned Judge of :the Tribunal found the accused guilty of the offence punishable under Sections 4(1) / 11 (Ka) of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 and awarded death penalty to him with an observation that it is a pure case of custodial death of the deceased where husband, the condemned-prisoner has not given any satisfactory explanation about the cause of death and the post-mortem report 'exhibit-3 also stands for injury which was antermortem and homicidal in nature. Beside such evidence the learned Judge of the Tribunal has alto relied upon the confessional statement of the accused vide Ext. 7 where he has depicted the lucid picture of the incident and his overact in the commission of the offence of murder of his wife. The Tribunal, however, acquitted others. 

 7. Mr. A. K. Bodrul Huq, the learned Senior Advocate, appearing for the petitioner, submits that the High Court Division erred in law in passing the impugned judgment and order affirming the sentence of death passed against the petitioner failing to find that confession-al statement of the petitioner as recorded by the learned Magistrate under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was involuntary, untrue as well as exculpatory, untrue, before recording the same the petitioner was kept for reflection under the care of the peon of the learned Magistrate, who was admittedly and Armed Police Constable, and further that in paragraph 4 of the certificate the learned Magistrate stated, "I have satisfied myself that there is no police officer in any place whence the proceedings can be seen or heard; except the above named ------ who has not been concerned in the investigation of the crime or in the arrest or production of the accused". Moreover the said confessional statement was exculpatory as the maker did not implicate himself in the commission of the alleged crime, more so, the same did not also corroborate with the post-mortem report concerning anti mortum injuries of strangulation to the neck of deceased. Learned Advocate submits that High Court Division did not take into consideration the answer of the accused while he was questioned whether he was tutored to make the confession by anybody, the accused answered in the affirmative, which fact itself made the confession inadmissible and because no time for reflection was mentioned in the body of the form for recording the Confessional Statement, which created suspicion whether at all any time for reflection was allowed. Mr. Huq submits that the High Court Division failed to take into consideration the very material fact that in the Charge sheet as many as 14 witnesses for the prosecution were named but 6 witnesses were withheld without any explanation given by the prosecution, for which the petitioner was prejudiced and was entitled to the benefit as could be available to him under section 114 (g) of the Evidence Act. He also submits that P.W. 2, Nasim Shaikh in his deposition during cross-examination   having stated that the petitioner made an extra judicial Confession to the police officer, which was recorded in a plain paper in presence of 40/50 local men including himself, which was neither brought to the notice of the learned court nor the same was at all taken into consideration by the High Court Division and therefore, there was a miscarriage of justice. 

 9. We have perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division carefully and anxiously. The learned Judges discussed and considered the facts, circumstances, evidence of witnesses and materials on record and found that in the instant case, there is no doubt about the custodial death of the wife where husband is to be considered main perpetrator of the crime observing that in such crime against newly wedded woman generally committed within the four walls of the house maintaining secrecy, independent witnesses or direct evidence is scarcely available to the prosecution. The High Court Division found that in such circumstances inculpatory confessional statement marked exhibit. 7 made by the appellate, which has not been denied is enough to find the accused guilty of the offence punishable under Section 11(Ka) of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 since demand of dowry as proved by the prosecution has not even been denied by the accused husband. In such facts and circumstances and evidence on record of the instant case, the learned Judges of the High Court Division dismissed the appeal accepting the Death reference upholding the conviction and sentence of the condemned-prisoner considering his confessional statement along with other circumstantial evidence like the custodial death of the wife and apprehension of the accused by the local people immediately after the occurrence and the confessional statement made by the accused husband within 2 days from the date of occurrence before the learned Magistrate, 1st Class. The impugned judgment having been passed on proper consideration and finding based on the evidence and materials on record, we do not find any reason to interfere with the same. The leave petition is thus dismissed having no substance.
